[[Deep North]] |Snow-capped hills and forests with frozen rivers, inhabited by [[Moose]], [[Elaking]], and [[Gammeltroll|Gammeltrolls]]. |Northern edge of the world |} == Alternative biomes == Each biome patch has a chance to have modifiers applied to it on world generation, but only a certain distance from the world center. These modifiers can have the following effects: * Affect foliage, like more [[Raspberries]] or only [[Birch]]es in the Meadows, or only stubs in the Black Forest * Generate additional structures, like [[Large Bone]]s in the Swamps, Plains or Mistlands, or more [[Tar Pit]]s in the Plains * Increase the chance for [[creature level|starred]] creatures * Enable the spawning of certain creatures not normally encountered in the biome, such as [[Bat]]s in the Swamp, or increase existing chances for a creature to spawn, like more [[Abomination]]s * Disable the spawning of creatures native to the biome Several modifiers can affect a single area at once. The following biomes can be affected: * [[Meadows#Alternative biomes|Meadows]] has 8 modifiers. * [[Black Forest#Alternative biomes|Black Forests]] have 8 modifiers. * [[Swamp#Alternative biomes|Swamps]] have 5 modifiers. * [[Mountain#Alternative biomes|Mountains]] have 3 modifiers. * [[Plains#Alternative biomes|Plains]] have 5 modifiers. * [[Mistlands#Alternative biomes|Mistlands]] have 6 modifiers. Oceans, the Ashlands and the Deep North do not have any alternative variants. ==Trivia== *The term "biome" comes from the [[wikipedia:biome|ecological concept of the same name]]. *At ''Valheim's'' early access launch in February 2021, five of the planned nine biomes were made available to explore. The other four were accessible, but lacked any meaningful content. ** As of the full release in September 2026, all biomes excluding the Ocean are fully implemented. An Ocean overhaul was ultimately abandoned, with the argument that it only serves the role of a highway between other biomes, which do have meaningful content. * Alternative biomes were introduced in the [[1.0]] release. {{Biomes}} [[de:Biom]] [[ru:Биомы]] [[pt-br:Biomas]] [[uk:Біоми]] [[cs:Biomy]] [[zh-tw:生物群落]] [[Category:Biomes| ]]

{{infobox biome | title = Swamp | image = Biome swamp.png | caption = | passive = * [[Giant Herring]] | hostile = * [[Blob]] * [[Oozer]] * [[Draugr]] * [[Draugr Elite]] * [[Leech]] * [[Skeleton]] * [[Surtling]] * [[Wraith]] * [[Writhan]] * [[Abomination]] | boss = [[Bonemass]] | unique = * [[Ancient Bark]] * [[Scrap Iron]] * [[Guck]] * [[Turnip Seeds]] | regular = | food = | structures = * [[Geyser]] * [[Abandoned Hut]] * [[Swamp Runestone Tower]] * [[Inverted Tower]] * [[Swamp Grave]] * [[Shipwreck]] | dungeons = [[Sunken Crypts]] | npcs = [[The Bog Witch]] }} The '''Swamp''' is an oppressive [[Biomes|biome]], filled with massive trees, muddy bogs, and hostile creatures. Immense, bare-branched [[Ancient Tree|Ancient Trees]] claw at a sickly cloud-laden sky, making for intimidating vistas. On what small bit of ground exists, tendrils of sodden soil snake around and through the knee-deep, plague-ridden water that permeates the entire biome. [[Draugr]] stumble about everywhere, watching and waiting to slay any living Viking they can find; to prove they are worthy of ascension to gods that have long since stopped listening. From a difficulty standpoint, the Swamps were designed to be a wall of sorts. Entering the biome for the first time, Vikings are met with an unprecedented drive by the very land to kill them as quickly and effectively as possible: every last creature here is hostile to the player. It is always raining in the mire regardless of the weather elsewhere; this means the player will always be [[Wet Effect|Wet]] when traversing the terrain. The toll taken on stamina in the Swamp is brutal, especially at night, when the player will also be [[Cold Effect|Cold]], and likely on the run from [[Wraith|Wraiths]]. The presence of [[Poison]] is undeniable as well, being the weapon of choice for [[Oozer]]s, [[Blob]]s, and [[Leech]]es. Making express use of a certain [[Poison Resistance Mead|mead]] unlocked in the previous biome is not negotiable. Sprinkling the landscape of any moderately large Swamp are [[Sunken Crypts]], which require a [[Swamp Key]] to unlock. These crypts sit in a state of near ruin, their winding corridors caved in and blocked by [[Muddy Scrap Pile]]s, which can be mined for [[Scrap Iron]], [[Leather Scraps]], and [[Withered Bone]]s. Up on the surface, half-submerged abandoned structures and [[Monster Spawner|hostile creature spawners]] can be found, as well as the occasional [[Geyser|Surtling Geyser]]. In addition to the Crypts, scrap piles can be found buried in the ground here. These waterlogged veins can be located using a [[Wishbone]] after defeating [[Bonemass]], though it should be noted that they tend to be uncommon and are generally not viable for providing any significant quantities of iron. Additionally, mining is a noisy activity and will attract the local fauna. == Creatures == ==== Hostile ==== * {{Item link|Blob}} * {{Item link|Oozer}} * {{Item link|Draugr}} * {{Item link|Draugr Elite}} * {{Item link|Leech}} * {{Item link|Skeleton}} * {{Item link|Surtling}} * {{Item link|Abomination}} * {{Item link|Wraith}} (night only) * {{Item link|Writhan}} * {{Item link|Seeker}} (at night after [[The Queen]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Charred Warrior}} (at night after [[Fader]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Charred Marksman}} (at night after [[Fader]] is defeated) ==== Passive ==== * {{Item link|Giant Herring}} == Resources == * {{Item link|Ancient Bark}} * {{Item link|Scrap Iron}} * {{Item link|Guck}} * {{Item link|Thistle}} * {{Item link|Turnip Seeds}} * {{Item link|Wood}} * {{Item link|Stone}} * {{Item link|Mushroom}} * Chests: (2-3 of the following) {{loot table| {{loot row|item=Amber |amt=1-5 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Amber pearl |amt=1-3 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Ancient bark |amt=20-30 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Chain |amt=1 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Coins |amt=20-60 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Ironhead arrow |amt=10-15 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Poison arrow |amt=10-15 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Ruby |amt=1-3 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Withered bone |amt=1 |rate=5.9%}} }} ==Alternative biomes== In addition to the regular [[Biomes]] generation, each local patch of biome has a chance to get an [[Alternative biomes]]. Once a Swamp is located, it is recommended that an adjacent [[Meadows]] or [[Black Forest]] is chosen for landfall. This way, it is significantly easier for a forward base to be erected and operated from. * There are various ways to glitch (i.e. through unintended ways) into a swamp crypt without using a key. These methods may be patched in later versions of the game. ** A popular strategy is to place a [[Chairs|chair]] just in front of the crypt entrance, sit in the chair, and then stand up. The player will be pushed through the gate and by extension, the loading barrier. ** The method listed above can also be utilized if a crypt is found to have an indestructible ancient tree blocking the entrance. == Gallery == Swamp1.jpg Swamp2.jpg Swamp Spawner.jpg Crypt 1.jpg Gravenimage.jpg|One of the statues found in the Swamp. The '''Smelter''' is a structure used to process certain raw metals into ingots.

== Building ==
It is be unlocked when the player acquires a {{Item link|Surtling Core}}. It must be constructed near a [[Workbench]].

Smelters can be placed directly onto terrain and stone structures. Currently, they cannot be placed on wood structures, but it is possible to bypass this to an extent by terraforming terrain with a [[Hoe]] to be in line with wooden floors.

== Usage ==
The Smelter is used to process certain raw materials into [[metal]] using {{Item link|Coal}} as fuel. Materials that can be smelted are:
{| class="wikitable"
! Ore !! Result

| {{Item link|Copper Ore}} || rowspan="2" | {{Item link|Copper}}

|-

|-

|-
| {{Item link|Iron Ore}}<ref group="Note"><small>Obtained via [[fishing]].</small></ref>

|}
<references group="Note" />

Ingots produced are dropped out in the '''front''' of the smelter, indicated by the angled chute. The smelter also requires free space on the '''left''' to be filled with ore and on the '''right''' to be filled with coal.

The Smelter uses 1 {{Item link|Coal}} every 15 seconds as fuel. It takes 30 seconds<ref><small>Ores used to take 31 seconds to smelt, but this was fixed in [https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/892970/view/3220644827970865344 update 0.208.1].</small></ref> to produce one bar of [[metal]].

It can hold a total of 20 Coal and 10 ores.

== Notes ==
* Like other structures that process materials, smelters are sped up with the passage of time that happens when the player is [[sleeping]].
* When destroyed with a [[Hammer]] or other means, it drops all materials used. It is therefore possible to alternate between using a Smelter and the [[Charcoal Kiln]], reconstructing them as needed.
* Smelters require adequate venting for the smoke above them, otherwise they will stop smelting.
* The smelter, while active, gives off the [[Fire Effect|Fire effect]] for about 4.5 meters from any side (not just the interaction point).
* Advanced metals have to be smelted using a [[Blast Furnace]] instead.

Populated [[Fuling Village]]s can be seen spread across the Plains, built from [[Deer Hide]] and [[Bone Fragments]]. Despite their initially tranquil appearance, the Plains biome is difficult and dangerous to navigate. The '''Charcoal Kiln''' is used to create [[Coal]] from wood. It converts single units of [[Wood]], [[Finewood]], or [[Corewood]] into coal at a rate of 1 every 15 seconds.

It can hold up to 25 wood at a time. When adding wood to the kiln, the game will prioritize wood from the player inventory in the following order:
# Wood
# Finewood
# Corewood

== Building ==
The Charcoal Kiln is unlocked when the player acquires a [[Surtling Core]]. A nearby [[Workbench]] is required to construct it.

Kilns can be placed directly onto terrain and stone structures. Currently, they cannot be placed on wood structures, but it is possible to bypass this to an extent by terraforming terrain with a [[Hoe]] to be in line with wooden floors.

== Notes ==
* Like other structures that process materials, Charcoal Kiln are sped up with the passage of time that happens when the player is sleeping.
* When destroyed with a [[Hammer]] or other means, it drops all materials used. It is therefore possible to alternate between using a [[Smelter]] and the Charcoal Kiln, reconstructing them as needed.
* Active kilns grant the [[Fire Effect]], providing players with heat as well as scaring away the appropriate monsters, albeit only 2 meters from all sides of it (not just the interaction point).

The '''Deep North''' is a vast, snowy [[Biomes|biome]], found in the northernmost part of ''Valheim''. Described as a "postcard of a Christmas landscape", it contrasts the hordes of the fiery [[Ashlands]] with fewer but stronger creatures.

Akin to the Ashlands, the Deep North landmass is separated from other biomes by an [[Ocean]] and borders the [[World Edge]] on the northern side. There is no equivalent of the boiling sea preventing access to the biome, however, defeating [[Fader]] is still required to progress through the biome, and strong enemies pose a threat. Sheets of ice float along the shores, a potential danger to any ship attempting to dock here.

As in the Mountains, all weather in the Deep North is freezing, day and night, so players without frost resistant clothes or [[Frost Resistance Mead]] in effect take continuous [[Freezing Effect|freezing]] damage outdoors. See [[#Weather|Weather]] below.

The biome was the focus of the [[Version history|1.0 update]].

Wind intensity is capped at 1. A blizzard's wind range lies above that cap, so the wind always blows at full strength during a blizzard.

A player outdoors and away from a fire gets the [[Freezing Effect|Freezing]] effect: no health regeneration, 60% slower stamina and eitr regeneration, and one point of damage every second. Near a fire or in shelter, the player gets the [[Cold Effect|Cold]] effect instead (50% slower health regeneration, 25% slower stamina and eitr regeneration), and a fire in shelter removes both. Slight, normal or very high frost resistance prevents both effects.

While it snows, snow builds up on structures that have no roof above them and are not inside a [[Shield Generator]]'s shield. It can be cleared with the [[Snow Shovel]].

'''Troll Caves''' are [[Points of Interest (POI)#Dungeons|dungeons]] found in [[Black Forest|Black Forests]]. 

== Description ==
They appear as large rock formations with a large entryway, usually decorated with two or three bone piles.

Troll caves have a 75% chance to have a [[Troll]] inside, and a 33% chance to have one outside the cave. Trolls do not respawn inside the cave, since they are a single-use [[Spawn points|spawn point]], nor do Trolls in the forest return to a cave. Trolls cannot enter or leave, and nothing other than the player can enter the cave, making an empty troll cave a completely safe refuge.  

It is possible to build a [[campfire]] inside a troll cave without being choked by smoke. The only other structures allowed are a [[Cooking Station]], a [[Sitting Log]], and a [[ward]] (the last of which would be useless, since the cave is classified as a dungeon and [[Workbench|workbenches]] cannot be placed there).

The '''Blast Furnace''' is a structure used to process advanced raw metals into ingots. Although it performs a similar function to the [[Smelter]], it cannot smelt the ores that the Smelter can.

== Building ==
It is unlocked after the player has killed [[Moder]] and built an [[Artisan Table]].

Blast Furnaces can be placed directly onto terrain and stone structures. Currently, they cannot be placed on wood structures, but it is possible to bypass this to an extent by terraforming terrain with a [[Hoe]] to be in line with wooden floors.

Unlike the Smelter, Blast Furnaces have both of their refueling ports to the left of the bar chute.

== Usage ==
The Blast Furnace is used to process certain raw materials into [[metal]] using {{Item link|Coal}} as fuel. Materials that can be smelted are:

It can hold a total of 20 Coal and 10 ores.

== Notes ==
* Like other structures that process materials, Blast Furnaces are sped up with the passage of time that happens when the player is sleeping.
* The Blast Furnace, while active, gives off the [[Fire Effect]] for about 3 meters from any side (not just the interaction point).

'''Frost Caves''' are [[Points of Interest (POI)#Dungeons|dungeons]] found in the [[Mountain]]s.

== Description ==
The entrance is composed of a spiky rock formation with large, blue icicles hanging from the roof of the cave mouth. These caves are the lairs of [[Cultist]]s, [[Ulv]]s, [[Bat]]s, and rarely [[Stone Golem]]s.

Bats lurk in deep shafts down into the mountain. Ulvs may be found in the icy caves or in worked-stone lairs with Cultists. Stone Golems can be found as a rare spawn in deep caves around an icy lake.

Frost Caves may also contain a [[Runestone|vegvisir]] that shows [[Moder]]'s nearest location.

The natural parts of the caves are dimly lit, with patches of light from cracks in the ceiling, or occasional standing torches by chests or altars. Glowing [[crystal]] formations may also be found on the floor and walls of the cave. [[Standing Brazier]]s can be found in the worked-stone portions of the caves and provide heat and light.

A rare feature that can spawn deep in the caves is a large frozen lake, guarded by one to three [[Stone Golem]]s. By the shore of this frozen lake the player can find a runestone left by a weary traveler, the remains of his campfire, and a [[Fishing Rod]] he left behind (which, when looted, also drops two to four [[Fishing Bait]]).

== Strategy ==
Walls of blue ice frequently block passages in the caves and will need to be broken. This can be done with any weapon, pickaxe, or even determined punching. Breaking these walls does create noise that will alert nearby creatures. These walls may not always hide a passage, but sometimes a plain cave wall or a stone with ancient markings. The ice walls have cracks in them that can give a hint to what lies beyond them if a player can peek through.  

One unique feature of Frost Caves are icicles hanging from the ceiling and growing up from the floor. They will break if struck by a powerful enough attack. Weapons will lose durability with these attacks, so swinging wildly may cause a lot more wear and tear on the player's gear. The icicles can be knocked loose from the ceiling, and will drop and do significant damage to anything below them with the same disregard for human life as a falling tree. This is the biggest concern when using [[Stagbreaker]] or an [[Iron Sledge]] in the Frost Caves.

A skilled archer can knock icicles down onto the heads of enemies instead of simply taking the easy route and shooting the enemy. Impaling enemies with falling icicles is challenging, but gratifying.

Another environmental peril of Frost Caves is the uncaring force of gravity. The caves frequently feature vertical shafts that may or may not have precarious paths down into them. Falling down one of these shafts will, of course, hurt. [[Bat]]s often spawn in these vertical shafts and in the chaos of their rapid fly-bys a careless character can find themselves baited by these flying creatures into a quick trip to the bottom. The good news is that if a player falls down into a hole that has no path up, there will be a way up from the bottom, just not the way they arrived. These shafts can be cleared with a running jump or sometimes have narrow ledges that will allow a cautious explorer to move by. 

The lairs of the [[Cultist]]s are behind wooden doors ([[Wood]] and sometimes [[Iron]] when destroyed), and feature a wide range of breakable objects, from furniture for [[Finewood]], to bones for [[Bone Fragments]], to tapestries of matted hair for [[Fenris Hair]]. The [[Red Jute]] curtains obscure vision, often hiding enemies. One strategy is to use an [[Iron Sledge]] to simply demolish everything, but this will obviously alert any inhabitants. These lairs may contain altars with Fenris hair and [[Fenris Claw]]s and Cultists, as well as rooms and corridors that can contain [[Ulv]]s. If Ulvs are detected, [[Ooze Bomb]]s are useful, since werewolves are vulnerable to poison. The tight corridors and poor sight-lines often make combat up close and personal, but a stealthy player may be able to use a bow in some areas. 

These lairs also feature piles of meat which have standard drop of [[Entrails]] with a chance to drop extra [[Coins]], [[Silver Necklace]] and [[Entrails]]. Altar rooms are the most rewarding, as they can have 0-4 jute and hair tapestries, with 0–5 additional knots of hair hanging beneath each one. The altar may have 2 or 4 offerings of Claws or hair, but they are guarded with 0–3 Cultists.

The '''Standing Brazier''' is a light source that can be placed on any surface, and must be built within the range of a [[Forge]].

==Usage==
The Standing Brazier has all the same functions as a [[Campfire]] and is a [[Player base|base]] structure.

Standing Braziers are fueled with [[Coal]]. With 1/5 fuel, a Standing Brazier will last for 5 hours and 33 minutes. At maximum capacity, a Standing Brazier should burn for 27 hours and 47 minutes. It can be used for cooking, however, it does not fit easily like a [[Campfire]] does.

The [[Fire Effect]] for the Standing Brazier extends for about 4–5 meters (Measured from the closest the player can stand without setting themselves on fire).

==Notes==
* Destroying the Standing Brazier with a [[Hammer]] will not yield back any [[Coal]] and will only return the 5 [[Bronze]] and 3 [[Fenris Claw]]s used for its construction. All Coal used as fuel and for the initial construction will <u>not</u> be dropped.
* Standing Braziers found in [[Frost Caves]] can be destroyed for Coal and sometimes Bronze.
* Standing Braziers stop working if exposed to rainy weather without a roof.

She is a monstrous [[Seeker]] Matriarch, and her appearance differs substantially from other Seekers. Her body is larva-like (similar to Seeker Broods), her four "arms" are all located nearer to the head, and she has a distinctive mouth lined with small, sharp teeth. Some features she shares with other Seekers are a set of large mandibles like the [[Seeker Soldier]], antennae like regular Seekers, and thin, wispy hair like both Seeker types. == Summoning == [[File:Infested Citadel.png|thumb|The entrance to The Queen's Lair, the Infested Citadel]] The Queen's [[Forsaken Altars|Forsaken Altar]] rests in the [[Mistlands]]. Unlike all previous bosses, she must be fought in a dungeon, the [[Infested Citadel]], and her first fight requires no sacrifice. The nearest Infested Citadel can be located by [[Runestone#Vegvisir|Vegvisirs]] found in [[Infested Mine|Infested Mines]], but entry requires a [[Sealbreaker]], which can be constructed from [[Sealbreaker Fragment|fragments]] also found in the mines. The Queen will spawn on the lower floor of the citadel and will wander around until aggroed. After her initial defeat, 3 [[Seeker Soldier Trophy|Seeker soldier trophies]] may be offered on the hive seat at the top of the citadel to summon her again. == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating the Queen|Boss strategies#The Queen}} === Teleport === Below 90% health and up to every 60 seconds, The Queen can burrow herself into the ground and emerge somewhere else within 200 meters. This ability is restricted to the [[Infested Citadel]] and to when a player is within 400 meters. === Rush === Below 60% health and within 5–25 meters of a player, The Queen can crawl in 16.24-meter line slashing her arms in an 8-meter 120-degree horizontal arc in front of her (100 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]], 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack has a cooldown of 25 seconds. === Bite === Below 70% health and within 10 meters of a player, The Queen can lunge forward and bite to inflict the [[Poison]] status (140 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]], 100 [[Damage types#Poison|Poison]], 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This reaches 10 meters from her center in a 25-degree horizontal arc. === Call === The Queen will stop and roar, which triggers holes within a 30-meter radius to spawn [[Seeker|Seekers]] and [[Seeker Brood|Seeker broods]]. Each hole is either a brood spawner or a regular Seeker spawner. The brood spawners have a 100% chance of hatching into Seeker broods, while the Seeker spawners have a 33% chance of hatching into Seekers and a 67% chance of hatching into Seeker Broods. A maximum of four Seeker broods and two Seekers can active from within a 50-meter radius of each hole - if this cap is reached the holes will not spawn any creatures. This ability is restricted to the [[Infested Citadel]] and she can still attempt to use it regardless of spawn caps. This ability has a 60-second cooldown, can be used when a player is within 25 meters, and is accessible while The Queen is below 99% health. === Spit === The Queen shoots 20 projectiles at the player which inflict the [[Poison]] and [[Slimed Effect|Slimed]] status (40 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 40 [[Damage types#Poison|Poison]], 50 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 50 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). Each projectile travels at 15 meters per second with a spread of 1–5 degrees. They can travel for 4 seconds before disappearing. When these projectiles make contact with the player or terrain, they explode and have a 30% chance each of spawning a [[Seeker Brood]]. A maximum of 30 Seeker broods can be active at once within the [[Infested Citadel]] (although the orange eggs scattered throughout the arena will not stop hatching after reaching the spawn cap). She can use this ability every 20 seconds when within 5–25 meters of a player and while below 80% health. === Slap === Within 9 meters of a player, The Queen swings one of her arms in front of her (130 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]], 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This hits in a 10-meter 145-degree horizontal arc in front of her. This attack can be used every 4 seconds. === Pierce AoE === The Queen stabs the ground nearby with all four arms dealing damage in a 4.5-meter radius circle around herself (150 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]], 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). She can use this attack every 4 seconds when a player is within 4 meters. == Aftermath == === Drops === {{drop table| {{drop row|item=Majestic carapace|0star=5}} {{drop row|item=The Queen trophy|0star=1}}|stars=0}} === Forsaken power === Mounting The Queen’s trophy upon her respective stone will allow you to claim her Forsaken Power. This ability will grant the player and nearby allies the following effects for 300 seconds: * Eitr regen: +100% * Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Resistant]] vs Poison * Sneak stamina usage: -100% === Creature spawning === Defeating The Queen unlocks [[Seeker]] to spawn at night in the [[Meadows]], [[Black Forest]], [[Swamp]], [[Mountain]] and [[Plains]], as well as unlocks [[Seeker Brood]] and [[Tick]] at night in [[Mistlands]]. Only [[Tick]]s can spawn with multiple stars. * Prior to [[Ashlands]] update, [[Tick]] and [[Seeker Brood]] could spawn in Meadows, Black Forest, Mountain and Plains, so this is currently unknown as bug or unannounced fix. === Events === Defeating The Queen affects the following [[events]] for that world: * Disables: "They sought you out." * Disables: "What's up, Gjall?!" * Enables: "The undead army marches" * Enables: "The dead have been summoned" === Traders === Defeating The Queen unlocks the [[Herbs of the Hidden Hills]] from [[The Bog Witch]] for 180 [[Coins]]. == Notes == * The entrance to the arena is completely safe from The Queen's attacks, enabling players to duck inside and heal. Note that the spawned Seekers and Broods will follow the player in, but no more will spawn until the player leaves and re-aggros The Queen. On occasion, The Queen's backend may stick through the wall into the entrance, enabling free hits. Upon leaving the entrance after some time, The Queen will always do a roar animation, allowing for a quick hit or two. * The Queen's health does not reset when players exit the citadel either voluntarily or through death, or when exiting the game. Instead, her health slowly replenishes over time, identical to other bosses or creatures. * The Slimed status effect is exclusive to The Queen's spit attack. * The Queen can easily be defeated by luring her to the entrance, then using the [[Demolisher]] to deal AOE damage. The Queen cannot hit you, and will die quickly. (Disabled in the latest patch: if the Queen can't reach the player character, she loses aggro and walks away. The luring mechanic can still be used in battle – shooting from a bow or an arbalest or throwing a spear at a wall lures her. Additionally, when her health bar disappears, the Queen can't aggro on the player character for about 20 seconds, so you can even attack her with a melee weapon.) == Gallery == File:Thequeensaltar.png File:Valheim Queen.png|The Queen In-game == Trivia == * The on-screen message that appears when The Queen spawns, "The Queen wants it all" is a reference to the 1989 song "I Want It All" by British rock band Queen. * The on-screen message that appears when The Queen is defeated, "Long live the Queen." * The Queen's unique drop was called "Queen drop" and was a placeholder before the Ashlands update. They look like huge, mutated [[Neck]]s. == Spawning == {{Spawn table|{{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Middle]] of the [[Ashlands]] during the daytime|limit=2|frequency=4|stars=Yes (max 1 star)}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Middle]] of the [[Ashlands]] during the nighttime, despawn at dawn|limit=2|frequency=4|stars=Yes}}}} == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Asksvin|Aggressive creature strategies#Asksvin}} Both before and after taming, Asksvin take no damage from [[lava]], despite not being immune to fire damage. === Bite === Sweeps their head back before rounding forward to chomp down on the player (75 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 75 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]], 50 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 50 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack hit in a horizontal arc of 5.5 meters and 45 degrees. It can be used every 4 seconds when within 3–6 meters of a player. The attack does high damage to [[Grausten Structures|grausten]] and weaker structures, similar to a Lox, and it can even damage [[Factions|allied creatures]]. == Aftermath == Defeating Asksvin allows the player to loot the following items. === Drops === {{Drop table|{{drop row|item=Asksvin trophy|0star=10%|1star=10%| 2star=10%}} {{drop row|item=Asksvin bladder| 0star=1|1star=2| 2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Asksvin hide| 0star=2|1star=4| 2star=8}} {{drop row|item=Asksvin tail| 0star=2|1star=4| 2star=8}}}} Parts for a buildable [[Asksvin Skeleton]] can also be found separately in the [[Ashlands]], but they drop from destroying Asksvin Skeletons already there, not from killing Asksvin. == Taming == ''For general taming information and strategies, see [[Taming]].'' Similar to the [[Wolf]], Level 3 (two-star) Asksvin only spawn at night. Like any creatures spawned at night, Level 3 Asksvin will attempt to flee the active area and despawn during daytime hours if the taming process has not begun. This can be prevented by either (A) trapping them in a pit or pen that they cannot escape (and staying within 64 meters of them) or (B) by starting the taming process, after which they will never despawn. Asksvin can be tamed by feeding them [[Smoke Puff]]s, [[Vineberry Cluster]]s or [[Fiddlehead]]s. They are rideable by equipping the [[Asksvin Saddle]]. When riding an Asksvin, players cannot attack. Players riding an Asksvin can traverse lava, and neither the player nor Asksvin will take damage from the lava. Tamed Asksvin do not do friendly fire damage to players, any other tamed creatures or neutral [[Dvergr (race)|Dvergr]]. == Breeding == Asksvin can breed, provided the Asksvin is happy and well-fed with [[Fiddlehead]] or [[Vineberry Cluster]] or [[Smoke Puff]], along with there being another Asksvin within four meters, and no more than 10 Asksvin within at least 10 meters. Once the conditions are met, they will accumulate love points with one another until the pregnancy starts. Pregnancy lasts 60 seconds, checked every 30 seconds, so the egg comes 60 to 90 seconds after it starts. They then lay an [[Asksvin egg]]. The quality of the Asksvin egg is determined by the Asksvin that laid it. A quality 1 egg in the player's inventory indicates a 0-star Asksvin, quality 2 indicates a 1-star, and quality 3 indicates a 2-star. Once laid, it would take 30 minutes to hatch into Asksvin Hatchling if there is a heat source nearby (Example [[Campfire]]). If the heat source is gone or the player puts the egg into their inventory, the timer is reset. Then the Asksvin Hatchling takes 50 minutes to grow into an adult without the need of heat source. They will not breed if the cap is reached, which is 10 Asksvin in 10 meters. However, there is currently no known limit to the eggs themselves. == Trivia == * The word "Asksvin" is Swedish for "ash swine." And like swine, the plural for Asksvin is the same as its singular form. * Due to their green and warty appearance, "Pickle-Dog" has gained popularity as a common moniker for Asksvin within the Twitch-Valheim community. {{Creatures}} [[uk:Попелозавр]] [[ru:Пеплозавр]]

6000 (gates) | tool tier = 5 |resources = * [[Loot chest#Charred Fortress Charred Chests|Charred chest]] * [[Bell Fragment]] * [[Molten Core]] | resistances = pickaxe only | number = 20 }} '''Charred Fortresses''' are [[Points of interest]] in [[Ashlands]]. They are marked by a beam of green light shooting straight up into the sky, visible from a distance. == Location == Each world has 20 Charred Fortresses. They are always located away from the coasts between the inland lava fields, usually inside the central islands of the Ashlands. == Layout == The fortress consists of a tall, rectangular outer wall with many pillars and spiked bronze defenses. Two opposing outer walls have closed gates in them, leading to the interior area. The interior contains an expanse of ground littered with gravestones, with two [[Effigy of Malice|Effigies of Malice]] in the corners and two stone ramps leading up to the parapets atop the exterior walls. In the very center of the fortress interior is a tall tower, capped with more spiked defenses, which has one gate leading inside. The walls (of the exterior and of the interior tower), the pillars, gates and spiked defenses can all be destroyed, but only by [[Damage#Pickaxe|Pickaxe damage of tool tier 5 or higher]] - i.e. a [[Battering Ram]] or a [[Catapult]] with [[Explosive Payload]]s. The pillars have negligible (1) health but the walls (1500), spikes (1500) and especially the gates (6000) have much higher health. The exterior walls are three layers thick, whereas the interior tower walls are only one layer thick. The fortress initially spawns some creatures, independently to the Effigies of Malice, they do not respawn if killed: * Up to 3 [[Charred Warlock]]s (100% chance for the one on top of the tower and 60% chance to spawn for the other). * Up to 5 [[Charred Marksman|Charred Marksmen]] (100% chance for the one on top of the tower and 60% chance to spawn for the other). * Up to 4 [[Skugg]]s (80% chance for each corner of the fortress to have one). == Loot == Inside the central tower can be found: * A Bell Altar, drops 2 to 4 {{Item link|Bell Fragment}}s when destroyed. * A [[Loot chest#Charred Fortress Charred Chests|Charred chest]]. * A [[Vegvisir|Fader Vegvisir]] with a 50% chance to spawn. * 2 [[Molten Core]]s. Other places inside the Fortress: * The interior court can have up to 8 [[Molten Core]]s, with a 5% chance each to spawn. * Up to 3 Charred chests can spawn along the solid walls of the tower (clockwise from the tower entrance: 100%, 13% and 50% chances to spawn). * [[Skugg]] drop {{item link|Charred Cogwheel}}s which allow the player to make a [[Catapult]]. * The bronze spike strips can be destroyed to drop 2-5 [[Scrap Bronze]] each. As each Charred Fortress contains exactly 78 spike strips, one fortress will yield an average of 273 scrap bronze. The content of Charred Chests is: {{Chest|Charred Chest}} == Notes == * The exterior walls (3 layers x 1500 health = 4500 total) are easier to break through than the gates (6000 health). The tower walls (1500 health) are easier still, but be careful not to accidentally destroy any loot (see below). * The Charred chests and the Bell fragment altar are destroyable; while the chests have 200 health and are resistant to most types of damage (except for [[Damage#Lightning|Lightning]], [[Damage#Poison|Poison]] and [[Damage#Spirit|Spirit]]), the altar is extremely fragile - having only 10 health and no damage resistances. * The presence of the Bell fragment altar is indicated by a huge vertical beacon of light, which can be seen at a distance. This beacon can help identify the location of intact fortresses from afar. ** Destroying the altar also removes the beacon. * The eastern and western smaller islands usually generate with no fortress, thus it is best to first land directly south of spawn. * Some segments of the walls can be mined with any pickaxe. This might be due to a bug. == Tips == * A simple strategy to conquer Charred Fortresses is to first master one Charred Fortress, obtain a [[Bloodstone]], and then craft the [[Trollstav]]. Now, the player can easily approach a Charred Fortress and summon [[Summoned Troll]]s from the outside, which will handle the fortress without any issues. Finally, kill the Troll and enjoy the loot! * It is easier to build a wooden ladder to get on top of the wall rather than using a [[Battering Ram]] to destroy the gates/walls. And, if you are lucky with the world generation, you could use one of the naturally spawning giant rocks to get inside too. Once on top of the walls, simply run circles in the walls and slowly kill enemies and destroy the [[Effigy of Malice|spawners]], if you get overwhelmed just jump off outside (be careful if there is lava). * You can destroy the [[Skugg|skuggs]] from outside the fortress with the bow/crossbow or magic, and from a high enough place you can also destroy the [[Effigy of Malice|spawners]] too. * If you conquered the fortress and didn´t destroy the walls/gates to get inside, the fortress is now a perfect place to build a mini base, thanks to the indestructible walls. Only the flying [[Fallen Valkyrie|valkyries]] and [[Volture|Voltures]] can get inside. * There are two ways to get inside the central tower without a [[Battering Ram]]. First is to make a hole on the ground with a pickaxe and simply pass below the wall of the tower (this may not work if you hit the limit on how low the ground can go). Second is to get on top of the tower and get inside through the hole between the spikes, to get out you will need to either portal out or build yourself ladders/platforms to pass through the hole between the spikes again. == Gallery == Charred fortress tower interior.png|The inside of a Charred Fortress tower.
